lesson.title: Multiply straight across
lesson.body: To multiply two fractions, multiply the numerators, then multiply the denominators: 2/3 × 3/4 = 6/12. Then write the answer in lowest terms: 6/12 = 1/2.

lesson.title: "Of" means times
lesson.body: 3/4 of 2/3 means 3/4 × 2/3. When both fractions are less than 1, the answer is smaller than both: you are taking a part of a part.

lesson.title: Improper fractions first
lesson.body: Write a whole number over 1, and change each mixed number to an improper fraction: 2 1/2 = 5/2. Multiply, then change the answer back to a mixed number in lowest terms.

lesson.title: A fraction of a whole number
lesson.body: To find 3/4 of 20, divide 20 into 4 equal parts and take 3 of them: 20 ÷ 4 = 5, and 3 × 5 = 15.

lesson.title: Of what is left
lesson.body: When the second fraction is of what is left, find what is left first. Then take the second fraction of that amount, not of the amount you started with.

lesson.title: Check it makes sense
lesson.body: Money left after spending must be less than you started with, and less than what was left after the first step.

lesson.title: How many fit?
lesson.body: 3/4 ÷ 1/8 asks how many eighths fit in three quarters. 3/4 is 6/8, so 6 of them fit.

lesson.title: Keep, flip, multiply
lesson.body: To divide by a fraction, keep the first fraction, flip the second one over, and multiply: 2/5 ÷ 3/4 = 2/5 × 4/3 = 8/15. The flipped fraction is called the reciprocal.

lesson.title: Wholes and mixed numbers
lesson.body: Write a whole number over 1 and change each mixed number to an improper fraction. Then keep, flip, multiply: 3 ÷ 3/4 = 3/1 × 4/3 = 4.

lesson.title: Bigger or smaller?
lesson.body: Dividing by a whole number shares, so the answer is smaller: 2/3 ÷ 4 = 1/6. Dividing by a fraction less than 1 counts how many fit, so the answer is bigger: 3 ÷ 3/4 = 4.

lesson.title: Take away first
lesson.body: When some is used before the rest is cut up or shared, take away what is used first. Then divide what is left.

lesson.title: Check by multiplying
lesson.body: 5 pieces of 3/4 m make 3 3/4 m, and with the 3/4 m bow that is 4 1/2 m, the length Nena started with.
